guarantees.claim: When xor_message is low, storage_d equals keccak_out.

When xor_message is high, for each share j in 0..Share-1 and each entry i in 0..DInEntry-1, the word slice storage_d[j][i*DInWidth+:DInWidth] is assigned storage[j][i*DInWidth+:DInWidth] XOR data_i[j] if the lower DInAddr bits of i equal addr_i; otherwise it is assigned storage[j][i*DInWidth+:DInWidth].

assumptions.claim: The width of data_i[j] must equal DInWidth. If narrower, the XOR will zero-extend; if wider, upper bits are ignored.
assumptions.risk: Zero-extension weakens XOR mixing and may cause unintended zero-padding; truncation discards critical data, compromising state integrity.

assumptions.claim: DInEntry must not exceed 2^DInAddr, otherwise multiple entry indices i share the same lower DInAddr bits and all will be updated simultaneously when addr_i matches that value.
assumptions.risk: Multiple state words are overwritten with the same data_i, violating the per-lane XOR invariant and corrupting the Keccak state.

assumptions.claim: The per-share width of storage/keccak_out must equal DInEntry * DInWidth; otherwise the slice i*DInWidth+:DInWidth may go out of bounds.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-range part-select produces X, corrupting the state and potentially leaking secret information during simulation or through synthesis quirks.

uncertain_points.claim: If DInWidth * DInEntry does not match the actual per-share bit width of the storage arrays, the slice i*DInWidth+:DInWidth can be out of bounds, causing X in the state. The design relies on an external assertion (WidthDivisableByDInWidth_A) but that may not be present in all flows.
uncertain_points.cond: Parameters set such that per-share width != DInEntry*DInWidth.
uncertain_points.risk: X propagation in state compromises hash integrity and may leak secrets in simulation or via hardware glitches.

uncertain_points.claim: If DInEntry exceeds 2^DInAddr, multiple entry indices i will have identical lower DInAddr bits, causing a single addr_i match to update all of them. This multi-write behavior is a legal parameter combination and may conflict with the intended one-entry-per-address model.
uncertain_points.risk: Unintended multi-lane XOR corrupts the Keccak state, leading to incorrect digest computation.

uncertain_points.claim: ICEBOX #18029 indicates that partial writes (when the total width is not divisible by DInWidth) are not handled; the chunk depends solely on the external assertion WidthDivisableByDInWidth_A. It is unclear whether the absence of in-chunk protection is acceptable for all integrations.
uncertain_points.cond: When the total width per share is not a multiple of DInWidth.
uncertain_points.risk: If the assertion is disabled or not enforced, partial-word accesses could cause misaligned XORs or X's, corrupting the state and potentially leaking secret material.
